summary.text: This briefing explores balancing safety alignment and instruction following in language models to prevent harmful compliance while preserving general capabilities using direct preference optimization. Simultaneously optimizing for safety and helpfulness often leads to internal conflicts or degradation in instruction-following capabilities. The proposed combination applies direct preference optimization to enhance safety analysis and guidance following initial reasoning content or structured safety training, ensuring that safety alignment is achieved while maintaining instruction-following performance.

jtbd.text: When deploying language models, the user wants to balance safety alignment and instruction following so that the model prevents harmful compliance without degrading general capabilities or suffering from internal conflicts.

value_prop.text: Applying direct preference optimization to enhance safety analysis and guidance helps maintain instruction-following performance while securing models against harmful queries and jailbreaks.

riskiest_assumption.text: The riskiest assumption is designated due to missing evidence on axis V (viability). Specifically, we assume that enterprise customers are willing to pay for an alignment solution that combines direct preference optimization with instruction-following safeguards.

mvp.text: To test the riskiest assumption regarding commercial viability, conduct customer interviews and a price acceptance test with a prototype alignment pipeline.
mvp.type: customer interviews and price acceptance test

success_metric.text: Achieve a proposed threshold of 40 percent positive pricing acceptance and confirmed willingness-to-pay from interviewed target organizations during the MVP phase.

kill_criteria.text: Terminate the project if fewer than a proposed threshold of 10 percent of interviewed prospective customers indicate a willingness to adopt or pay for the DPO-based safety alignment tool.
